Overview

Helsinki as a Business Centre

Helsinki is Finland's capital and its dominant business centre. The city had about 694,000 residents at the end of 2025 and the Helsinki Region about 1.62 million, with roughly 804,000 jobs and more than 163,000 business establishments across the region. Services account for almost 89 percent of jobs in the city. The largest private employers include Nordea, ABB and the cooperative retailer HOK-Elanto, and the capital region concentrates Finland's corporate headquarters, financial institutions and listed companies. The Port of Helsinki handled about 10 million passengers in 2025, largely on routes to Tallinn and Stockholm, and Helsinki Airport about 17 million.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Helsinki because it is the entry point for most investment into Finland and much of the Nordic-Baltic trade. Foreign-owned companies generate around a quarter of turnover in the Helsinki region, with Swedish, US, German and UK owners most prominent, so acquirers and partners need reliable background on Finnish targets and management. Technology and engineering businesses raise intellectual property and departing-employee questions. Finland's long border and historic trade with Russia mean some Helsinki-registered companies have ownership or supply links that require careful sanctions review. Commercial disputes are frequently arbitrated in Helsinki under the rules of the Finland Chamber of Commerce.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Helsinki

01

Technology and software acquisition diligence

Background research on Helsinki technology, gaming and software companies, their founders and key engineers ahead of acquisitions or investments, covering corporate history, related companies, litigation, insolvency records and reputation, so buyers understand who they are acquiring and what risks travel with the business.

02

Eastern ownership and sanctions review

Tracing shareholders, directors and trading relationships of Helsinki-registered companies with historic Russian or Belarusian links, using Finnish registers and open sources, to support compliance counsel assessing sanctions exposure, ownership changes made after 2022 and possible circumvention through intermediaries in the Nordic-Baltic region.

03

Baltic trade counterparties

Verifying logistics, trading and distribution companies that operate on the Helsinki-Tallinn and wider Baltic Sea routes, including the consistency of their Finnish and Estonian registrations, management overlaps and dispute histories, where invoicing, VAT or cargo irregularities are suspected.

04

Arbitration fact-finding support

Assembling factual records for counsel in arbitrations administered by the Finland Arbitration Institute or other Helsinki-seated proceedings, including counterparties' corporate structures, prior disputes, financial filings and publicly disclosed assets relevant to the merits and to later enforcement.

05

Internal misconduct at Nordic headquarters

Supporting counsel investigating suspected conflicts of interest, procurement irregularities or expense fraud at Helsinki-based headquarters of Nordic groups, focusing on lawful background research into vendors and related parties and on scoping inquiries consistent with Finnish employee privacy rules.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Helsinki

Finland Arbitration Institute

The Arbitration Institute of the Finland Chamber of Commerce (FAI), based in Helsinki, is the leading and by far the largest arbitration institution in Finland. Its current Arbitration Rules came into effect on 1 January 2024, and it also offers expedited rules. Arbitration in Finland is governed by the Arbitration Act (967/1992), which a government proposal submitted in June 2026 would amend from spring 2027.

Courts sitting in Helsinki

The Helsinki District Court is the country's largest first-instance court and handles a large share of Finland's commercial litigation, insolvency matters and set-aside actions for awards made in Helsinki. Appeals go to the Helsinki Court of Appeal, and the Supreme Court also sits in the city. The Market Court, which hears competition, public procurement and intellectual property cases, is located in Helsinki as well.

Registries and the business ID

Finnish companies across the country are registered with the Finnish Patent and Registration Office, and basic data is searchable through the business information system using the Business ID. For Helsinki matters, extracts, filed financial statements and director details are the starting point, supplemented by insolvency, enforcement and court records and by Finnish-language business press.

Financial centre institutions

Helsinki hosts Nasdaq Helsinki, the Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority and the Bank of Finland, as well as the Nordic head office of Nordea. Exchange releases, insider disclosures and supervisory sanctions decisions provide useful public records on listed companies, financial firms and their management.

Bilingual and multilingual records

Finnish and Swedish are both official languages, and some Helsinki companies and court records use Swedish. About 21 percent of Helsinki residents have another mother tongue, most commonly Russian, Somali, Arabic, English or Estonian. Effective research uses Finnish, Swedish and, where relevant, Russian and Estonian sources.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Helsinki

For matters touching Helsinki, TDSC first defines the decision or dispute the work must serve, such as an acquisition, a sanctions question or an arbitration, and then identifies which Finnish registers, court records and exchange disclosures are relevant. Research is conducted from Nashville in Finnish, Swedish and English, with Russian and Estonian sources added where ownership or trade links extend east or across the Gulf of Finland. Where interviews, document retrieval or local enquiries are justified, TDSC coordinates with appropriately authorised Finnish professionals and the client's counsel rather than acting directly. Personal data is processed under the GDPR and Finnish law with a defined purpose, and employee-related enquiries are scoped with counsel.

TDSC has no office in Helsinki. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Helsinki: Frequently Asked Questions

Can you check whether a Helsinki company still has Russian ownership links?

We trace current and historic shareholders, directors and signatories through Finnish registers, filed accounts and open sources, and look for ownership changes, nominee arrangements and related companies in neighbouring jurisdictions. We report what the records show and what is inferred, so the client's sanctions counsel can reach a conclusion. We do not access restricted government or bank data.

How do you support an arbitration under the Finland Arbitration Institute rules?

We provide counsel with sourced factual research on the opposing party, its group structure, related entities, financial position, prior disputes and assets that may matter for enforcement. We do not contact tribunal members or witnesses improperly, and procedural and legal questions remain with Finnish or international counsel.

Are Finnish company records easy to use?

Basic company data is accessible and identified by a Business ID, and financial statements are generally filed with the registry. The challenge is often language and context: records may be in Finnish or Swedish, and groups may span Sweden or Estonia. We read the sources in their original language and connect entities across borders.

Can you investigate an employee at our Helsinki office?

Finnish law places firm limits on processing employee data and on monitoring communications. We help counsel scope inquiries lawfully, typically by researching vendors, related companies and public records rather than personal communications. Any review of company systems is directed by counsel and the employer under applicable law, not conducted covertly by TDSC.

Does TDSC have an office in Helsinki?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Helsinki or elsewhere in Finland. Most work is desk-based research. Where local steps are needed, we coordinate with appropriately authorised Finnish professionals and the client's counsel, and we decline requests involving pretexting, covert surveillance or access to restricted records.
